items.title: Ruth Brown interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: Freddie Green, that was his life. I saw him, he said, “Well Basie’s gone I don’t know what I’m gonna do.”

ctx.x: Freddie Green, that was his life. I saw him, he said, “Well Basie’s gone I don’t know what I’m gonna do.” And sure enough. But he sat there for over 40 years playing that [scats] that was the Basie band, you see? The simpler, the better. The simpler, the better. And of course Basie, he was such a wonderful individual. You know and I think the thing about those days that was really great was there was no competitiveness. Whatever was

good for the show, that’s what we did. We toured together, we rode the buses together, we lived under the same circumstances, we ate under the same circumstances, and when you went to the stage at night, it was a combined effort, you know? It wasn’t about who can outdo the other. It’s like here, we’re here as a unit, let’s make those people who bought the tickets glad they came, and let’s have them ask when we will be back again, you know. I think that was the thing that I remember most about it, you know. And I…
